Enjoying this newsletter? Get it in your inbox every weekend, as well as our daily round-up of The Economist’s best journalism, by signing up for free here. The forces under Donald Trump’s command put their feet up over the weekend. It has been three days since America launched new strikes against Iran, following 13 nights of back-and-forth attacks. The calm may not last. On Friday Mr Trump was threatening a return to full-scale war. Our new article looks at his options; few of them are good.  The longer the war goes on, the higher oil prices are likely to go. Some analysts see them topping the level of $139 a barrel reached in 2022, after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Similar predictions at the start of the Iran war did not pan out. But this time energy markets are more precarious. Bo Franklin, Senior digital editor What to expect in the week ahead: ▸ Meta and Microsoft will announce their quarterly results on Wednesday. Both companies’ share prices have fallen of late; investors are worried about their spending on AI. Apple reports on Thursday. A recent surge in its stock price saw it overtake Nvidia as the world’s most valuable company.  ▸ A big day of diplomacy awaits Donald Trump on Tuesday. He is expecting visits from Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukraine’s president, and Binyamin Netanyahu, Israel’s prime minister. Both leaders are also reported to be attending the funeral of Lindsey Graham, a Republican senator from South Carolina, on the same day.  ▸ The Federal Reserve will announce its latest interest-rate decision on Wednesday. Lorie Logan, one of the Fed’s rate-setters, has said rates should rise because “inflation has been too high for too long”, but the bank is generally expected to leave rates unchanged at next week’s meeting. The Bank of England will deliberate on interest rates on Thursday. Two of the nine members of its Monetary Policy Committee voted to raise rates at its previous meeting. Editor's picks America has few good options for a “massive attack” on Iran For the first time in nearly two weeks, America has not launched new strikes against Iran in the past 48 hours. The lull comes after 13 consecutive nights of American bombing and 12 attacks by Iran on ships in the Persian Gulf since July 6th, essentially shutting the Strait of Hormuz once more. 76545.subject: Stripe is paying $10 billion for OpenRouter’s 5.5% fee, not its LLM routing 🤖💸; Revolut is officially worth $115…
76545.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1104

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Monday! Today, we’re diving into payments giant Stripe, which is now in talks to buy OpenRouter for a whopping $10 billion (what this M&A is all about, why it’s very strategic for Stripe, & how it differs from Ramp’s LLM routing approach + bonus deep dive into the AI Monopoly Playbook [ https://substack.com/redirect/b7c1a85d-ed08-4ba4-80e7-7559843d5428?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and How to Build an Agentic OS with Claude Fable 5 [ https://substack.com/redirect/6783c50d-a67f-4828-985e-42f3dc47e0cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), and Revolut that’s now officially worth $115 billion, thus making it the 8th most valuable bank in Europe (why it matters, where’s the biggest risk & opportunity for Revolut + bonus deep dives into Revolut, Monzo, and Starling’s latest financials [ https://substack.com/redirect/3287c9fd-032d-4630-becc-3d0cfdaad039?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and Revolut’s Foundation AI Model [ https://substack.com/redirect/d1ddfd06-bcce-4b93-bd0c-1928fb682c46?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside). So let’s jump straight into the fascinating stuff 🌶️
Stripe is paying $10 billion for OpenRouter’s 5.5% fee, not its LLM routing 🤖💸
The BIG News 🔥 FinTech giant Stripe is currently in talks to buy OpenRouter for around $10 billion, roughly eight times the $1.3 billion valuation the AI model marketplace carried in May 😳 And everyone who covered the deal so far framed it as a payments company buying the routing layer for AI. OpenRouter’s own pricing page says otherwise.
Let’s take a closer look at this to understand what this M&A is actually all about - the 5.5% fee that is OpenRouter’s entire revenue line, why Stripe’s own AI Gateway couldn’t get there, how Ramp is running the identical product in reverse [ https://substack.com/redirect/a7a3bfe0-389a-4a87-858f-e049a6bcb125?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and the one number that tells you whether $10 billion is smart...

Unsubscribe https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5hcy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWN0aW9uL2Rpc2FibGVfZW1haWw_.VTTbyunPAYxnGFgG_9mwUflXJfwLcpQiLRY6xtisa8M?
